# Fault-Tolerant Bounded Flow Preservers

**Shivam Bansal** \(\unknown\)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Delhi, India

**Keerti Choudhary** \(\unknown\)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Delhi, India

**Harkirat Dhanoa** \(\unknown\)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Delhi, India

**Harsh Wardhan** \(\unknown\)

Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT Delhi, India

**Abstract**

Given a directed graph G=(_V,E_) with _n_ vertices, _m_ edges and a designated source vertex \(s\in V\) , we consider the question of finding a sparse subgraph H of G that preserves the flow from _s_ up to a given threshold \(\lambda\) even after failure of _k_ edges. We refer to such subgraphs as \((\lambda,k)\)-fault-tolerant bounded-flow-preserver \(((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP). Formally, for any \(F\subseteq E\) of at most _k_ edges and any \(v\in V\) , the (_s,v_)-max-flow in H\\_F_ is equal to (_s,v_)-max-flow in G\\_F_, if the latter is bounded by \(\lambda\), and at least \(\lambda\) otherwise. Our contributions are summarized as follows:

1. We provide a polynomial time algorithm that given any graph G constructs a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G with at most \(\lambda 2^kn\) edges.

2. We also prove a matching lower bound of \(\Omega(\lambda 2^kn)\) on the size of \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP. In particular, we show that for every \(\lambda,k,n\ge 1\), there exists an _n_-vertex directed graph whose optimal \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP contains \(\Omega(min\{2^k\lambda n,n^2\})\) edges.

3. Furthermore, we show that the problem of computing approximate \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP is NP-hard for any approximation ratio that is better than \(O(log(\lambda^{-1}n))\).

**2012 ACM Subject Classification** Theory of computation \(\rightarrow\) Data structures design and analysis; Mathematics of computing \(\rightarrow\) Graph algorithms

**Keywords and phrases** Fault-tolerant Data-structures, Max-flow, Bounded Flow Preservers

### 1 Introduction

We address the problem of computing single-source fault-tolerant bounded-flow-preservers for directed graphs. The objective is to construct a sparse subgraph that preserves the flow value up to a parameter \(\lambda\) from a given fixed source _s_, even after failure of up to _k_ edges.

The following definition provides a precise characterization of this subgraph.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Definition 1.** _Let_ G=(_V,E_) _be a directed graph and_ \(s\in V\) _be a designated source vertex. A_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-Fault-Tolerant Bounded-Flow-Preserver_ \(((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP_) _for_ G _is a subgraph_ \(\mathcal{H}=(V,E_\mathcal{H}\subseteq E)\) _of_ G _satisfying that for every_ \(F\subseteq E\) _of at most k edges, and every_ \(t\in V\) ,

\(max_{-flow}(s,t,\mathcal{H}-F)=\left\{\begin{array}{ c c }
max_{-flow}(s,t,\mathcal{G}-F) & \text{\textit{if}}max_{-flow}(s,t,\mathcal{G}-F)\le\lambda, \\
\text{\textit{At least}}\lambda, & \text{\textit{otherwise.}}
\end{array}\right.\)

For the special case of \(\lambda=1\), the problem is referred to as _k_-Fault-Tolerant Reachability Subgraph (_k_-FTRS) in the literature. Here the goal is to preserve reachability from _s_ after _k_ edge failures. Baswana et al. [4] showed that there exists a _k_-FTRS with at most 2_<sup>k</sup>n_ edges. Lokshtanov et al. [17] presented an algorithm for computing a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP for directed graphs. Their algorithm runs in time \(O(4^{k+\lambda}(k+\lambda)^2(m+n)\cdot m)\), and each vertex of the

## 2 Fault-Tolerant Bounded Flow Preservers

FT-BFP has in-degree at most \(4^{k+\lambda}(k+\lambda)\). They also showed that a \((k+\lambda-1)\)-FTRS of a graph G also serves as it’s \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP. Using this result in conjunction with the algorithm from [4], they obtain an alternate construction of a \((k,\lambda)\)-FT-BFP with at most \(2^{k+\lambda} n\) edges. However, this bound is quadratic in _n_ for any \(\lambda\) larger than log_n_.

We consider the problem of obtaining a tight bound on \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP. Specifically, we aim to answer the following question:

_Given a directed graph_ G=(_V,E_) _with a source s, and a flow threshold_ \(\lambda\ge logn\)_, can we construct a_ sparse \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP_ \(\mathcal{H}=(V,E_H\subset E)\)_? If so, can we present graphs for which the construction turns out to be tight?_

In this paper, we affirmatively answer the question above. We provide construction for FT-BFP that has a linear dependence on \(\lambda\). In particular, we prove the following.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 2.** _There exists an algorithm that for any directed graph_ G _on n vertices and m edges, and any integers_ \(\lambda,k\ge 1\)_, computes in_ \(O(\lambda 2^kmn)\) _time a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for_ G _with at most_ \(\lambda 2^kn\) _edges._

Furthermore, we show that the extremal bound of \(\lambda 2^kn\) in the above construction is tight by presenting the following lower bound.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 3.** _For every_ \(\lambda,k,n\ge 1\)_, there exists a construction of an n-vertex directed graph whose optimal_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP contains_ \(\Omega(min\{2^k\lambda n,n^2\})\) _edges._

We next consider the problem of approximating \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP structures. We show that unless _P=NP_, there is no polynomial-time algorithm to obtain a \(log(\lambda^{-1}n)\) approximation to optimal \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 4.** _For any_ \(\lambda,k,n\ge 1\) _satisfying_ \(k=\Omega(log(\lambda^{-1}n))\)_, the problem of computing an_ \(O(log(\lambda^{-1}n))\) _approximate_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for n vertex digraphs is NP-hard._

We finally present application of our FT-BFP construction in computing all-pairs fault- tolerant \(\lambda\)-reachability oracle.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 5.** _Given any directed graph_ G=(_V,E_) _on n vertices and any positive constants_ \(\lambda,k\ge 1\)_, we can preprocess_ G _in polynomial time to build an O(n_<sup>2</sup>) _size data structure that, given any query vertex-pair_ (_x,y_) _and any set F of k edges, reports the_ \((x,y)\lambda\)_-reachability in_ G\\_F in O(n_<sup>1+_o_(1)</sup>) _time._

## 1.1 Existing Works

For undirected graphs, there exists a tight construction for \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP with \(O((k+\lambda)\cdot n)\) edges that directly follows from \(\alpha\)-edge connectivity certificate constructions provided by Nagamochi and Ibaraki [19].

A closely related problem to that of graph preservers is fault-tolerant reachability oracles. For dual failures, the work of [11] obtained an _O(n_) size single source reachability oracle with constant query time for directed graphs. Brand and Saranurak [23], showed construction of an \(\widetilde{O}(n^2)\) sized _k_-fault-tolerant all-pairs reachability oracle that has \(O(k\omega)\) query time.

Recently, Baswana et al. [2] considered the problem of sensitivity oracle for reporting max- flow value for a single source-destination pair. They presented an _O(n_<sup>2</sup>) size data-structure that after failure of any two edges, reports the max-flow value of the surviving graph in constant time.

For the problem of computing the value of all-pairs max-flow up to \(\lambda\) in the static setting, Abboud et at. [1] obtained two deterministic algorithms that work for DAGs: a combinatorial algorithm which runs in \(O(2^{O(\lambda^2)}\cdot mn)\) time, and another algorithm that can be faster on dense graphs which runs in \(O((\lambda logn)4^{\lambda+o(\lambda)}\cdot n^\omega)\) time.

Some other graph theoretic problems studied in the fault-tolerant model include computing distance preservers [12, 21, 20], depth-first-search tree [3], spanners [8, 13], approximate single source distance preservers [5, 22, 6], approximate distance oracles [14, 9], compact routing schemes [9, 7].

Given a digraph G=(_V,E_) on _n_=|_V_| vertices and _m_=|_E_| edges, we first define some notations used throughout the paper.

We next define the concept of farthest min-cut that was introduced by Ford and Fulkerson in their pioneering work on flows and cuts [15]. Let _S_ be a source set, and _t_ be a destination vertex. Any (_S,t_)-cut _C_ is a partition of the vertex set into two sets: _A(C_) and _B(C_), where \(S\subseteq A(C)\) and \(t\in B(C)\). An (_S,t_)-min-cut _C_<sup>∗</sup> is said to be the _farthest min-cut_ if \(A(C^*)\unknown A(C)\) for every (_S,t_)-min-cut _C_ other than _C_<sup>∗</sup>. We denote the cut _C_<sup>∗</sup> by FMC(_S,t,_G). Similar to farthest-min-cut, we can define the nearest min-cut. An (_S,t_)-min- cut _C_<sup>∗</sup> is said to be the _nearest min-cut_ if \(A(C^*)\unknown A(C)\) for every (_S,t_)-min-cut _C_ other than _C_<sup>∗</sup>. We denote the cut _C_<sup>∗</sup> by NMC(_S,t,_G).

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Property 6.** _Let s be a source vertex, t be a destination vertex, and f be an s to t max-flow in graph_ G_. Let_ G<sub>f</sub> _denote the residual graph corresponding to flow f. Further let X be the set of vertices reachable from s in_ G<sub>f</sub>_, and Y be the set of vertices having a path to t in_ G<sub>f</sub>_. Then NMC(s,t,_G)=(_X,V_\\_X_) _and FMC(s,t,_G)=(_V_\\_Y,Y_).

We prove in this section the following hardness result for approximating optimal FT-BFP.

## 2 Preliminaries

in(_v,_G): The set of in-neighbours of _v_ in G.

out(_v,_G): The set of out-neighbours of _v_ in G.

In-Edges(_v,_G): The set of all incoming edges of _v_ in G.

Out-Edges(_v,_G): The set of all outgoing edges of _v_ in G.

out(_A,_G): The set of all those vertices in _V_\\_A_ having an incoming edge from some vertex of _A_ in G, where \(A\subseteq V(\mathcal{G})\).

G(_A_): The subgraph of G induced by the vertices lying in a subset _A_ of _V_.

G+(_u,v_): The graph obtained by adding an edge (_u,v_) to graph G.

G\\_F_: The graph obtained by deleting the edges lying in a set _F_ from graph G.

max-flow(_S,t,_G): The value of the maximum flow in graph G from a source set _S_ to a destination vertex _t_. When the set _S_ comprises of a single vertex, say _s_, we represent it simply by max-flow(_s,t,_G).

path[_a,b,T_]: The path from node _a_ to _b_ in a tree _T_.

_P[a,b_]: The subpath of path _P_ lying between vertices _a_ and _b_, where _a_ precedes _b_ on _P_.

_P_\(\circ Q\) : The path formed by concatenating paths _P_ and _Q_ in G. Here it is assumed that the last edge (or vertex) of _P_ is the same as the first edge (or vertex) of _Q_.

## 3 Hardness of logarithmic approximation

## 4 Fault-Tolerant Bounded Flow Preservers

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 7.** _For any_ \(\lambda,k,n\ge 1\) _satisfying_ \(k=\Omega(log(\lambda^{-1}n))\)_, the problem of computing an_ \(O(log(\lambda^{-1}n))\) _approximate_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for n vertex digraphs is NP-hard._

We prove the above theorem by showing a reduction from the SET-COVER problem to the optimal FT-BFP.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Problem 8** (\[18\], Definition 1)**.** _The input to SET-COVER consists of base set U,_ |_U_|=_n and subsets_ \(S_1,\dots,S_m\subseteq U\), \(\cup_{j=1}^mS_j=U\), \(m\le poly(n)\)_. The goal is to find as few sets S_<sub>_i_<sub>1</sub></sub>_,...,S<sub>i<sub>k</sub></sub> as possible that cover U, that is,_ \(\cup_{j=1}^kS_{i_j}=U\)

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 9** (\[18\], Theorem 2)**.** _For every_ \(0<\alpha<1\) _(exact) SAT on inputs of size n can be reduced in polynomial time to approximating SET-COVER to within_ \((1-\alpha)lnN\) _on inputs of size_ \(N=n^{O(1/\alpha)}\).

From Lemma 9, we can also deduce that it is NP-Complete to approximate SET- COVER up to a multiplicative factor of _c_<sub>1</sub>logmax(_n,m_) for some _c_<sub>1</sub>_\>_0 as \(m\le poly(n)\).

**Transformation** Given a SET-COVER instance \(\langle U,\mathfrak{F}\rangle\), we will construct a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT- BFP instance \(\langle\mathcal{G},s\rangle\). The transformation is as follows (also see Figure 1).

**1.** Round up the number for elements in _U_ to nearest power of 2 (let this be 2_<sup>u</sup>_) by adding 2_<sup>u</sup>_-|_U_| new elements to _U_ and all these new elements to every set in F.

**2.** Initialize G to be the graph with _N_+1 vertices, namely, _s,v_<sub>1</sub>_,...,v<sub>N</sub>_ where \(N=4\lambda(m+n)\).

**3.** Next construct the following subgraph G_<sub>i</sub>_, for each \(i\in[1,\lambda]\).

**a.** Construct a complete binary tree _B<sub>i</sub>_ rooted at a vertex _r<sub>i</sub>_ of height _u_ and 2_<sup>u</sup>_ leaf nodes. The leaf nodes of _B<sub>i</sub>_ will correspond to elements in the universe _U_. From each leaf node _x<sub>i</sub>_ in _B<sub>i</sub>_, add out-edges to two new vertices, namely, \(\ell(x_i)\) and _r(x<sub>i</sub>_).

**b.** For each set \(W\in\mathfrak{F}\), add a vertex _y<sub>i,W</sub>_ to graph G_<sub>i</sub>_. Let _Y<sub>i</sub>_ denote the resulting set which consists of |F| vertices. For each \(x\in U\) and \(W\in\mathfrak{F}\), add an edge from \(\ell(x_i)\) to _y<sub>i,W</sub>_ if and only if \(x\in W\).

**c.** Add a set _Z<sub>i</sub>_ of _u_+1 additional vertices. For each leaf _x<sub>i</sub>_ in _B<sub>i</sub>_, add an edge from _r(x<sub>i</sub>_) to each vertex in the set _Z<sub>i</sub>_.

**4.** Finally, we add an edge from _s_ to the roots \(r_1,\dots,r_\lambda\). Also for each \(i\in[1,\lambda]\), we add an edge from each vertex in \(Y_i\cup Z_i\) to each of the vertices _v_<sub>1</sub>_,...,v<sub>N</sub>_.

We set _k=u_+1 for this \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP instance.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 10.** _Any_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP_ H _of the graph instance_ \(\langle\mathcal{G},s\rangle\)_, can be used to construct a solution of the SET-COVER instance of size at most_ \(\lambda^{-1}(min_{j=1}^N|_{IN}(v_j,\mathcal{H})|)\).

**Proof.** Consider a vertex _v<sub>j</sub>_ in H that minimizes |IN(_v<sub>j</sub>,_H)|. Consider the following candidate solutions

\(S_i=\{W\in\mathfrak{F}|(y_{i,W},v_j)\in E(\mathcal{H})\}.\)

Out of the \(\lambda\) sets, namely \(S_1,\dots,S_\lambda\), let _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> be the set with least cardinality. The cardinality of _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> is at most \(|in(v_j,\mathcal{H})|/\lambda\) as minimum value is upper-bounded by the average value.

Now in order to prove that _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> is a valid solution, consider an element \(x\in U\). Let _P_ be the unique path from _r_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> to leaf node _x_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> in _B_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>, and let _F_<sub>1</sub> be the set of all those edges \((u,v)\in B_{i_0}\) such that \(u\in P\) and _v_ is the child of _u_ not lying on _P_. Observe that _x_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> is the unique leaf in _B_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> that is reachable from _s_ in H\\_F_<sub>1</sub>. Let _F_<sub>2</sub> be a singleton set comprising of the edge (_x_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>_,r(x_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>)). Consider the set \(F=F_1\cup F_2\) of size _k_. Since

max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_G\(\backslash F\)) = \(\lambda\), there must exists a path, say _Q_, from _s_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ in H\(\backslash F\) passing through _r_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>. Such a path _Q_ must pass through \(\ell(x_{i_0})\) as well as a vertex in _Y_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>, say _y_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub>_,W_</sub>. This implies that the edge (_y_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub>_,W_</sub>_,v<sub>j</sub>_) lies in H, and so by definition of _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>, the set _W_ lies in _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>. Moreover _W_ contains the element _x_ as \((\ell(x_{i_0}),y_{i_0,W})\) is an edge in G. This proves that element \(x\in U\) is covered by _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub>, and thus _S_<sub>_i_<sub>0</sub></sub> is a valid solution to \(\langle U,\mathfrak{F}\rangle\). \(\blacktriangleleft\)

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 11.** _Any solution S of the SET-COVER instance_ \(\langle U,\mathfrak{F}\rangle\)_, can be used to construct a solution_ H _of_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP instance satisfying_ \(|\mathrm{in}(v_j,\mathcal{H})|=\lambda(|S|+k)\)_, for each_ \(j\in[1,N]\).

**Proof.** Let _S_ be a solution of the SET-COVER instance \(\langle U,\mathfrak{F}\rangle\). Consider the sets

\(A_i=\{y_{i,W}|W\in S\}\cup Z_i,\text{for}i\unknown\lambda,\text{and}A=\bigcup_{i=1}^\lambda A_i.\)

We will show that

\(\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{G}\backslash\cup_{j=1}^N\mathrm{In}\text{-Edges}(v_j)+\cup_{j=1}^N(A\times v_j).\)

is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G.

Let us assume, to the contrary, that H is not a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G. Then there must exist an edge set _F_ of size at most _k_ and an index \(j\in[1,N]\) satisfying max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_G\(\backslash F\)) is greater than max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_H\(\backslash F\)). Observe that each path from _s_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ must pass through a vertex _r<sub>i</sub>_, for some \(i\in[1,\lambda]\), and each _r<sub>i</sub>_ only allows a unit flow to pass through it.

Since max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_G\(\backslash F\))_\>_max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_H\(\backslash F\)), there must exist an index \(i\in[1,\lambda]\) satisfying that there exists a path from _s_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ in G\(\backslash F\) _passing through r<sub>i</sub>_, but no such corresponding path exists in H\(\backslash F\).

Let \(R=\{x_i^0,x_i^1,\dots,x_i^\alpha\}\) be the set of leaf nodes in tree _B<sub>i</sub> reachable_ from _s_ in G\(\backslash F\). There exist at least min(_k_+1,|_R_|) vertex-disjoint paths from _R_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ in H, namely,

\((\{x_i^0,\ell(x_i^0),y_{i,W},v_j)\text{, where}W\in\mathfrak{F}\text{is the set in}S\text{that contains the element}x^0\in U.\)

\((\{x_i^c,r(x_i^c),z_i^c,v_j)\text{, for}c=1\text{to min}(k,|R|-1).\)

Thus even after _k_ faults atleast one path from _r<sub>i</sub>_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ will exist in H\\_F_. This contradicts the assumption that there is no _s_ to _v<sub>j</sub>_ path in G\\_F_ passing through _r<sub>i</sub>_. Hence, max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_G\\_F_) must be identical to max-flow(_s,v<sub>j</sub>,_H\\_F_). \(\blacktriangleleft\)

The proof of Theorem 7 now directly follows from Lemma 9, Lemma 10, and Lemma 11, along with the fact that for every integer \(n\ge 1\), there exist hard instances of the SET- COVER problem (_U,_F) satisfying |_U_|=_n_, where the size of the optimal solution is significantly larger than log|_U_|.

## 4 Upper bound of \(\lambda 2^kn\) Edges

In this section we will provide construction of a sparse \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP.

### 4.1 Locality Property for Flow Preservers

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 12.** _Let_ G=(_V,E_) _be a graph with a source_ \(s\in V\), \(\lambda\ge 1\) _be an integer, and v be a vertex in V. Let_ \(\alpha=min\left(\lambda,max-flow(s,v,\mathcal{G})\right)\)_. Let_ E_<sub>v</sub> be the set of in-edges of v corresponding to any arbitrary set of_ \(\alpha\)_-edge-disjoint paths from s to v in_ G_. Further, let_ H _be a subgraph of_ G _obtained by restricting the in-edges of v to those present in_ E_<sub>v</sub>. Then, for any vertex_ \(t\in V\),

\(max-flow(s,t,\mathcal{H})\ge min\left(\lambda,max-flow(s,t,\mathcal{G})\right).\)

**Proof.** By construction of _H_, \(\alpha=max-flow(s,v,H)\). Denote \(\beta=max-flow(s,t,H)\). Let (_A,B_) be an (_s,t_)-min-cut in _H_. If \(v\in A\) then, by construction of _H_, the (_s,t_)-cut (_A,B_) has value \(\beta\) also in _G_, so \(\beta\ge max-flow(s,t,G)\) and we are done. Assume next \(v\in B\). Then (_A,B_) is an (_s,v_)-cut of value \(\beta\) in _H_. By construction of _H_, \(\alpha=max-flow(s,v,H)\), so \(\beta\ge\alpha\). If \(\alpha=\lambda\) we are done, so assume \(\alpha=max-flow(s,v,G)\).

We now show that \(\beta\ge max-flow(s,t,G)\), which ends the proof. Suppose not, and let _f_ be an (_s,t_)-max-flow in _H_. Then the residual graph _G<sub>f</sub>_ must have an augmenting path _P_, containing some edges present in _G_ but not in _H_. Such edges are all incoming to _v_. Thus, \(P=P[s,w]\circ(w,v)\circ P[w,t]\) where \((w,v)\in E(G)\backslash E(H)\), and _P[s,w],P[v,t_] are present in the residual graph _H<sub>f</sub>_. Adding _P_ to _f_ gives an (_s,t_)-flow of in _H_+(_w,v_), implying that

**1.** max-flow(_s,t,H_+(_w,v_))=\(\beta+1\)

**2.** \((w,v)\in A\times B\)

**3.** (_A,B_) is an (_s,t_)-min-cut in _H_+(_w,v_)

Let \(\{Q_i\circ e_i\circ Q'_i\}_{i=1}^\alpha\) be \(\alpha\) edge-disjoint _s_-to-_v_ paths in _H_, where the edge _e<sub>i</sub>_ of each such path is its last edge crossing the (_s,v_)-cut (_A,B_), so \(V(Q'_i)\subseteq B\). Such exist as \(\alpha=max-flow(s,v,H)\). Let \(e_{\alpha+1},\dots,e_\beta\) be the other edges crossing (_A,B_) in _H_. Let _e_<sub>0</sub>=(_w,v_), crossing (_A,B_) by (ii). Let \(\{P_j\circ e_j\circ P'_j\}_{j=0}^\beta\) be \(\beta+1\) edge-disjoint _s_-to-_t_ paths in _H_+(_w,v_), each crossing the cut (_A,B_) exactly once, at _e<sub>j</sub>_, so \(V(P_j)\subseteq A\). Such exist by (i) and (iii). Then, \(\{P_0\circ e_0\}\cup\{P_i\circ e_i\circ Q'_i\}_{i=1}^\alpha\) are \(\alpha+1\) edge-disjoint _s_-to-_v_ paths in _G_, contradicting \(\alpha=max-flow(s,v,G)\). \(\blacktriangleleft\)

In the next lemma we show that in order to compute a sparse \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP it suffices to focus on a single destination node.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 13** (Locality Lemma for Flow Preservers)**.** _Let_ A _be an algorithm that given any graph_ G _and any vertex_ \(v\in V(\mathcal{G})\)_, computes a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP of_ G _with at most_ \(c_{\lambda,k}\) _in-edges to v. Then using_ A_, one can construct for any n vertex digraph a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP with at most_ \(c_{\lambda,k}\cdot n\) _edges._

**Proof.** Consider a graph G with _n_ vertices, namely, _v_<sub>1</sub>_,...,v<sub>n</sub>_. We will provide a construction of \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G using black-box access to algorithm A. We compute a sequence of graphs G<sub>0</sub>,G<sub>1</sub>_,...,_G_<sub>n</sub>_ as follows:

1. Initialize G<sub>0</sub>=G. 2. For \(i\ge 1\), compute G_<sub>i</sub>_ in two steps: **a.** First use A to compute a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G<sub>_i_-1</sub> in which the in-degree of _v<sub>i</sub>_ is bounded by \(c_{\lambda,k}\), let this graph be H<sub>_i_-1</sub>. **b.** Obtain G_<sub>i</sub>_ from G<sub>_i_-1</sub> by restricting the incoming edges of _v<sub>i</sub>_ to those present in H<sub>_i_-1</sub>. It is easy to verify that the in-degree of each vertex in G_<sub>n</sub>_ is at most \(c_{\lambda,k}\). To show that G_<sub>n</sub>_ is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G, it suffices to show that G_<sub>i</sub>_ is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G<sub>_i_-1</sub>, for each \(i\ge 1\). Let us fix an index _i_ in the range [1_,n_]. Consider a set _F_ of at most _k_ edges in G<sub>_i_-1</sub>, and let \(\alpha=min\big(\lambda,\text{max-flow}(s,v_i,\mathcal{G}_{i-1}\backslash F)\big).\) By construction, H<sub>_i_-1</sub> is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G<sub>_i_-1</sub>, so there exists at least \(\alpha\) edge-disjoint paths from _s_ to _v<sub>i</sub>_ in the graph H<sub>_i_-1</sub>\\_F_. Let E_<sub>i</sub>_ be the set of in-edges of _v<sub>i</sub>_ corresponding to these \(\alpha\) edge-disjoint paths. Observe that the edges in E_<sub>i</sub>_ lie in graph G_<sub>i</sub>_\\_F_. Moreover, graphs G_<sub>i</sub>_\\_F_ and G<sub>_i_-1</sub>\\_F_ differ only at in-edges of _v<sub>i</sub>_. Therefore by Lemma 12 it follows that for any vertex \(t\in V(G)\), \(\text{max-flow}(s,t,\mathcal{G}_i\backslash F)\ge min\big(\lambda,\text{max-flow}(s,t,\mathcal{G}_{i-1}\backslash F)\big)\). This proves that G_<sub>i</sub>_ is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G<sub>_i_-1</sub>. \(\blacktriangleleft\)

## 4.3 Computing sparse \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP

In this subsection, we will show how to construct a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G from a (_k+f_-1)- FTRS of G. We will start by introducing a lemma from [17], followed by additional lemmas that will help us to obtain a tight construction for FT-BFP.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 18** ([17])**.** _Let_ G _be a directed graph with a designated source node s, and let_ H _be a_ \((k+\lambda-1)\)_-FTRS of_ G_. Then,_ H _is also a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP of_ G.

To strengthen the above lemma, we present a method for constructing a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT- BFP from a \((min\{f,\lambda\}+k-1)\)-FTRS, where _f_ represents the maximum flow from the source node _s_ to a destination node _t_ in the graph.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 19.** _Let_ G _be a directed graph with a designated source node s, and let t be a vertex satisfying_ max-flow(_s,t,_G)=_f, for some positive integer f. Then a_ \((min\{f,\lambda\}+k-1)\)_- FTRS of_ G _that differs from_ G _only at in-edges of t is a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for_ G. **Proof.** Let H be a \((min\{f,\lambda\}+k-1)\)-FTRS of G that deviates from G only at in-edges of _t_. It follows from Lemma 18 that the subgraph H is a \((min\{f,\lambda\},k)\)-FT-BFP for G. The claim trivially holds true if \(f\ge\lambda\), so let us consider the scenario \(f<\lambda\). Consider a set _F_ of at most _k_ edge failures in G, and let _p_ be max-flow(_s,t,_G\\_F_). Since \(p\le f<\lambda\) and H is a (_f,k_)-FT-BFP, the max-flow from _s_ to _t_ in H\\_F_ must be exactly _p_. Since G and H only differs at in-edges of _t_, it follows from Lemma 12 that for each \(v\in V(\mathcal{G})\), max-flow\((s,v,\mathcal{H}\backslash F)\ge min(\lambda,max-flow(s,v,\mathcal{G}\backslash F))\). This proves that H is a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP for G. We now provide construction of a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP that bounds the in-degree of a single destination node _t_. \(\blacktriangleright\) **Lemma 20.** _Let_ G _be an n vertex, m edges directed graph with a designated source node s, and t be any arbitrary vertex in_ G_. Then for any_ \(\lambda,k\ge 1\)_, we can compute in_ \(O(2^k\lambda m)\) _time a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for_ G _in which the in-degree of t is bounded above by_ \(2^k\lambda\). **Proof.** Let _f_=max-flow(_s,t,_G). We present a construction of a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP, say H, by considering the following two cases. Case 1. max-flow\((s,t,\mathcal{G})\ge\lambda+k\):
Let us start by taking a look at the scenario \(f\ge\lambda+k\). In this case we can choose any \(\lambda+k\) incoming edges of _t_ which carry a flow of \(\lambda+k\) from _s_ to _t_ and discard all other incoming edges of _t_ to construct H. The resulting graph H will be a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G due to Lemma 19, and the in-degree of _t_ in H will be \(\lambda+k\le 2^k\lambda\). Case 2. max-flow\((s,t,\mathcal{G})<\lambda+k\):
We next consider the case \(f<\lambda+k\). In this case we use Theorem 14 to compute a \((min\{f,\lambda\}+k-1)\)-FTRS of G, say H0, such that the in-degree of _t_ in H0 is at most \(2^kmin\{f,\lambda\}\). We obtain the graph H from G by limiting the incoming edges of _t_ to those present in H0. The resulting graph H will be a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G due to Lemma 19. We conclude with the following theorem that directly follows by combining together Lemma 13 and Lemma 20. \(\blacktriangleright\) **Theorem 21.** _Let_ G _be an n vertex, m edges directed graph with a designated source node s. Then for any_ \(\lambda,k\ge 1\)_, we can compute in_ \(O(2^k\lambda mn)\) _time a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-FT-BFP for_ G _in which the in-degree of every vertex is bounded above by_ \(2^k\lambda\). ## 5 Matching Lower Bound We shall now show that for each \(\lambda,k\), \(n(n\ge 3\lambda 2^k)\), there exists a directed graph G with _O(n_) vertices whose \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP must have \(\Omega(2^k\lambda n)\) edges. The construction of graph G is as follows. Let \(B_1,\dots,B_\lambda\) be vertex-disjoint complete binary trees of height _k_ rooted at vertices _r_1_,...,rk_, and let _s_ be a new vertex have an edge to each of the _ri_’s. Let _X_ denote the set of leaf nodes of these \(\lambda\) trees, and let _Y_ be another set containing \(n-\sum_{i=1}^\lambda|V(B_i)|-1(\ge n/3)\) vertices. Then the graph _G_ is obtained by adding an

edge from each \(x\in X\) to each \(y\in Y\) . In other words, \(V(G)=\{s\}\cup V(B_1)\cup\cdots\cup V(B_\lambda)\cup Y\) and \(E(G)=\{(s,r_i)|1\le i\le\lambda\}\cup E(B_1)\cup\cdots\cup(B_\lambda)\cup(X\times Y)\).

We prove in the following lemma that any \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of the above constructed graph contains at least \(\Omega(2^k\lambda n)\) edges.

**Proof.** It is easy to see that the out-edges of _s_, and the edges of each of the binary tree _B<sub>i</sub>_’s must be present in a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G. Thus, let us consider an edge \((x,y)\in X\times Y\) , where _x_ is the leaf node of some binary tree _B<sub>i</sub>_.

Let _P_ be the unique path from _r<sub>i</sub>_ to _x_ in _B<sub>i</sub>_, and let _F_ be the set of all those edges \((u,v)\in B_i\) such that \(u\in P\) and _v_ is the child of _u_ not lying on _P_. On failure of set _F_, there remains a unique path from _s_ to _y_ that passes through edge (_s,r<sub>i</sub>_). Moreover, max-flow\((s,y,\mathcal{G}\backslash F)=\lambda\). So, any subgraph H of G not containing (_x,y_) edge would not be a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP as on failure set _F_, H would not preserve (_s,y_)-max-flow.

Hence, any \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G contains at least \(|X\times Y|=2^k\lambda|Y|\ge 2^k\lambda n/3\) edges.

## 6.2 FT-BFPs for graphs with non-unit capacities

We have shown till now that for any digraph G with unit capacities, one can compute a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP with \(O(2^k\lambda n)\) edges. We shall now show how to extend this result to a digraph with integer edge capacities such that flow values up to \(\lambda\) are preserved under bounded capacity decrement.

Let us first formalize the notion of FT-BFP under capacity decrement function.

\(\blacktriangleright\) **Definition 24.** _Let_ G=(_V,E,c_) _be a directed flow graph such that capacity of any edge is a positive integer, and let_ \(s\in V\) _be a designated source vertex. A subgraph_ \(\mathcal{H}=(V,E_0\subseteq E)\) _of_ G _is said to be a_ \((\lambda,k)\)_-Fault-Tolerant Bounded-Flow-Preserver if for any capacity decrement function_ \(I:E(G)\rightarrow\mathbb{N}\) _satisfying_ \(\sum_{e\in E(G)}I(e)\le k\)_, the following holds for the capacity function c_<sup>∗</sup> _defined as c_<sup>∗</sup>(_e_)=_c(e_)-_I(e), for_ \(e\in E\)_: For every_ \(t\in V\) ,

\(max-flow(s,t,\mathcal{H}|c^*)=\left\{\begin{array}{ c c } max-flow(s,t,\mathcal{G}|c^*) & \text{\textit{if}}max-flow(s,t,\mathcal{G}|c^*)\le\lambda, \\ At least\lambda, & \text{\textit{otherwise}}; \end{array}\right.\)

_where,_ H|_c_<sup>∗</sup> _and_ G|_c_<sup>∗</sup> _are respectively the graphs_ H _and_ G _with capacity function c_<sup>∗</sup>.

Let us now discuss the construction of \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFPs. Let G=(_V,E,c_) be a digraph with integer edge capacities. We first transform G into a multigraph G<sup>∗</sup> by replacing an edge (_x,y_) of capacity _c(x,y_) by exactly _c(x,y_) copies of edge (_x,y_) of unit-capacity. Thus, for vertex \(v\in V\) , the _s_ to _v_ max-flow in graphs G and G<sup>∗</sup> are identical.

Now, let H<sup>∗</sup> be a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of multigraph G<sup>∗</sup>. Then, a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G, say H=(_V,E_<sub>0</sub>_,c_), can be obtained by simply retaining all those edges whose multiplicity in H<sup>∗</sup> is non-zero. The graph H will indeed be a \((\lambda,k)\)-FT-BFP of G since a bounded capacity decrement in G corresponds to _k_-edge failures in G<sup>∗</sup>.
